title: 1964 Savage Mountain B-52 crash
summary: On 13 January 1964, a B-52D carrying two nuclear weapons was returning to Georgia from Massachusetts. Near Meyersdale, Pennsylvania, after altitude changes to evade severe winter storm turbulence, the vertical stabilizer broke off in flight. The aircraft became uncontrollable and the crew bailed out. Three of five crew members died; the radar bombardier died in the crash and two others died of exposure in the snow.

title: 1964 T-39 shootdown incident
summary: An unarmed T-39 Sabreliner training aircraft departed Wiesbaden Air Base on 28 January 1964 on a routine training flight. Forty-seven minutes after takeoff, the aircraft drifted into East German airspace with its radio systems malfunctioning, preventing response to warnings from U.S. air defense stations. Two Soviet MiG-19 fighters intercepted the aircraft. After approaching for eleven minutes without radio response, one MiG fired on the T-39 and it crashed near Erfurt. All three crew members died as direct casualties of the Cold War.
probable_cause: The T-39's radio systems malfunctioned and the crew were unable to respond to warnings. The aircraft drifted into East German territory where Soviet fighters intercepted and fired upon the unarmed trainer, which crashed.

factors.evidence: a MiG-19 jet fighter of the Soviet Air Force fired on the aircraft
the T-39's radio systems malfunctioned and the crew were unable to respond
radar at two U.S. air defense stations noticed that the trainer was heading toward East Germany at 500 mph
the aircraft disappeared from radar after Soviet interceptors approached

events.text: An unarmed USAF North American T-39A Sabreliner twin engine jet trainer 62-4448 of the 7101st Air Base Wing departed Wiesbaden Air Base at 14:10 hours on a routine three-hour training flight.
Forty-seven minutes after takeoff, radar at two U.S. air defense stations noticed that the trainer was heading toward East Germany at 500 mph.
Each air defense station began hailing the plane on USAF frequencies and a Soviet-monitored international distress band but repeated calls went unanswered.
The T-39 crossed the border into East Germany.
Two blips appeared near the American jet on radar for 11 minutes, indicating Soviet interceptors were approaching.
Radar blips indicated the three planes were moving eastward together for 11 minutes without response to radio calls.
Two radar blips suddenly veered west and the third blip disappeared, indicating the T-39 had been shot down by a Soviet interceptor.
The T-39 crashed in open farmland approximately 20 km north of Erfurt near Vogelsberg in East Germany.

title: Eastern Air Lines 304
summary: Eastern Air Lines Flight 304 crashed into Lake Pontchartrain five minutes after departing New Orleans en route to Atlanta. The investigation revealed that the horizontal stabilizer had been trimmed to the full nose-down position to counter an excessive nose-up attitude caused by a malfunctioning pitch trim compensator that had extended too far. Once the aircraft entered an upset in turbulence, the crew was unable to recover because the severe G-forces from pulling back prevented trimming the stabilizer back.
probable_cause: Degradation of aircraft stability characteristics in turbulence caused by abnormal longitudinal trim component positions, specifically a malfunctioning pitch trim compensator that extended excessively.

factors.evidence: A malfunctioning pitch trim compensator had extended too far, causing an excessive nose-up attitude

The breakup was so extensive that only 60 percent of the wreckage was recovered

title: Alitalia 45
summary: A Vickers Viscount 785D on approach to Naples International Airport at 10:36 PM encountered poor weather with cloud coverage at 2000-3000 feet and visibility 6 km. The aircraft descended to 4000 feet on a visual approach and struck the slopes of Mount Somma. Investigation found that an unaccounted for westerly wind pushed the aircraft toward Vesuvius, weather was worse than forecast at airport, and the pilot may have had excessive confidence from prior operations at Naples.
probable_cause: The weather conditions in the area surrounding the airport were variable and worse than those at the airport itself. An unaccounted for westerly wind pushed the Viscount towards Mount Vesuvius while the pilot had presumably planned an approach taking into account the southerly wind indicated in the field bulletin. Possible excessive confidence of the pilot in his knowledge of the orographic characteristics of the area contributed.

title: Pacific Air Lines 773
summary: Fairchild F-27 Flight 773 crashed near San Ramon, California after a suicidal passenger shot both pilots in the cockpit. Francisco Paula Gonzales, experiencing financial and marital difficulties, had announced his suicidal intent to multiple people before the flight. The shooting caused loss of aircraft control and fatal impact. Civil air regulations were amended following this incident to require cockpit doors be kept locked in flight.
probable_cause: The shooting of the captain and first officer by a passenger during flight.

factors.evidence: Investigators found in the mangled wreckage a damaged Smith & Wesson Model 27 .357 Magnum revolver, holding six spent cartridges.
The plane crashed, killing all 44 aboard.
Gonzales had informed both relatives and friends that he would die on either Wednesday, the 6th of May, or Thursday, the 7th of May.
The FBI determined that the suicidal Gonzales was the shooter.
Civil air regulation amendments requiring that doors separating the passenger cabin from the crew compartment must be kept locked in flight became effective following the crash.
An exception to the rule remains during takeoff and landing on certain aircraft, such as the Fairchild F-27, where the cockpit door leads to an emergency passenger exit.
The amendments were passed by the Federal Aviation Administration prior to the crash of Flight 773, but had not yet become effective.

events.text: The evening before the crash, Gonzales showed the gun to numerous friends at the airport and told one person that he intended to shoot himself.

title: United Airlines 823
summary: United Airlines Flight 823, a Vickers Viscount with 39 occupants, crashed near Parrottsville, Tennessee on 9 July 1964 after an uncontrollable in-flight fire of undetermined origin. Fire developed in the passenger cabin during cruise, causing loss of control and forcing descent. One passenger attempted to escape through the No. 4 window but died in the free-fall. The Civil Aeronautics Board was unable to identify the source of fuel, ignition point, or cause of the final maneuver, concluding only that an uncontrollable fire resulted in loss of aircraft control.
probable_cause: An uncontrollable in-flight fire of undetermined origin in the fuselage resulted in loss of control of the aircraft.

The aircraft crashed and burned; about 33,000 pounds of wreckage were recovered from the 40,000 pound aircraft.
The investigation addressed potential problems with the Pyrene Duo Head Model DCD-10 fire-extinguisher system for underfloor compartments; an Airworthiness Directive was issued.

title: Aeroflot 721
summary: Aeroflot Flight 721, an Ilyushin Il-18V, crashed into a hill during approach to Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk in poor visibility and clouds. The crew initiated descent prematurely and did not have sufficient knowledge of approach conditions. During the approach turn, the crew descended below the minimum safe altitude of 900 meters for terrain clearance. Eighty-seven of 93 people on board were killed.
probable_cause: Pilot error and poor in-flight planning; the crew initiated descent prematurely and apparently did not have sufficient knowledge of approach conditions.

factors.evidence: Clouds were present in the area and visibility was limited to 10 km.

The crew forgot that the minimum altitude for entering the turn was 1200 m and they should not have exited the turn at an altitude lower than 900 m in order to avoid colliding with a mountain ridge in the area at 790 m.
The crew apparently did not have sufficient knowledge of approach conditions and initiated descent prematurely without maintaining proper altitude awareness.
The aircraft crashed into the side of a hill on approach to Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, killing 87 of the 93 people aboard.

title: Flying Tiger Line 282
summary: Flying Tiger Line Flight 282 crashed on Sweeney Ridge shortly after takeoff from San Francisco on 24 December 1964 in heavy fog and rain.
